competitions.result: Fourth round — lost 1–0 away to Peterborough United.
Quarter-final — lost 4–1 on aggregate to Genoa.

overview: Liverpool finished sixth in the First Division in Graeme Souness’s first full season, 18 points behind champions Leeds United, but won the FA Cup. Michael Thomas and Ian Rush scored in the 2–0 final victory over Sunderland. Ronnie Moran deputised during Souness’s recovery from heart surgery in the closing weeks of the campaign.

The squad changed substantially: Dean Saunders and Mark Wright arrived from Derby County, Mark Walters from Rangers and Rob Jones from Crewe. Peter Beardsley, Steve Staunton and Steve McMahon were among those who left. Saunders finished as leading scorer with 23 competitive goals, nine of them in the UEFA Cup.

Liverpool returned to European competition after six years away, opening with a 6–1 home win over Kuusysi Lahti. They overturned a 2–0 first-leg deficit against Auxerre with a 3–0 Anfield victory, but Genoa eliminated them in the quarter-finals. Peterborough United ended their League Cup run in the fourth round.

The UEFA Cup fourth round was the quarter-final. Souness remained the appointed manager during his health absence; Moran is identified as his deputy rather than a permanent replacement. No disputed claim about who exclusively managed the final is made.
The LFChistory Souness narrative incorrectly begins the European run with Auxerre. The complete fixtures and dedicated European history establish Kuusysi as the first-round opponents.
managerNote: Souness remained manager. Moran deputised during his recovery from heart surgery in April and May.
